subject: Deploy mode needs: traffic shape & latency targets
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastledger.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deploy mode needs: traffic shape & latency targets

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the narrow questions we need to qualify the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

1) Traffic shape: average QPS, 95th/99th percentile spikes, and typical burst duration (minutes).
2) Latency targets: p95 and p99 for token-complete responses (end-to-end).
3) Request profile: chat (multi-turn) vs single-turn completion; average tokens in prompt + response.
4) Compliance/network: any requirement for VPC-only or on-prem?
5) Pilot timeline and procurement constraints (PO date, VM approvals).

Attached a quick template (traffic_profile.csv) and an SLA matrix draft to capture targets. If you can populate the CSV with a day-of-week sample or a 24h window we can run a quick capacity sketch and a cost/latency tradeoff.

Initial guidance based on what you said on the call: if peak sustained >500 QPS we usually recommend Dedicated; if you have very bursty microbursts (x10 baseline for short windows) we need to look at burst capacity and fallback policies.

Next steps proposed:
- You share the traffic_profile.csv sample and any SLOs (p95/p99) by Wed 3/10.
- We run a simulated burst microbenchmark and share a one-page recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated + estimated monthly committed capacity).
- Align on pilot scope (2-week pilot) and target PO date.

Thanks — I looped Ben and Marissa to help size the pilot.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastledger.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform@fastledger.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 18:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deploy mode needs: traffic shape & latency targets

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap. I'm attaching a sampled 24h export and a short note inside traffic_profile.csv (two sheets: baseline-hourly, burst-examples). High-level answers below so you can start sizing:

- Average QPS (sustained): ~120 QPS (business hours).
- Peak burst: we see short bursts up to ~1.8k QPS for ~3–6 minutes every ~40–60 minutes (these are user-initiated search spikes).
- p95 target: 150 ms end-to-end; p99 target: 350 ms (hard requirement during business hours).
- Request profile: chat-style UI but average tokens per request is small: prompt ~30 tokens, response ~50 tokens (we often use short context + recent turns).
- KV/prefix caching: we have a lot of repeated prefixes (search suggestions) — would expect caching to help, but unsure of cache-hit ratios (can provide logs).
- Compliance: must run in a VPC and provide audit logs, but not strictly on-prem yet.
- Timeline: pilot in 4 weeks; procurement needs an LOE and a rough cost ballpark by 3/17. PO target: 2027-04-10.

Questions for you: can Redwood support the burst profile without a dedicated reserved pool? If not, what minimal committed capacity would you recommend to hold p99 under those bursts? Also please confirm us-east availability.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | FastLedger
sanjay@fastledger.com

Attachment: traffic_profile.csv (2 sheets)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastledger.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deploy mode needs: traffic shape & latency targets

Thanks Sanjay — this is perfect for a sizing pass. A few calibration notes and the recommendation path we typically follow given this profile: 

1) Short summary of fit:
- Hosted API: likely meets p95 at baseline/steady QPS (120 QPS), and works well with caching. But given the 1.8k QPS microbursts, unreserved Hosted could see headroom shortages and p99 spikes unless we do aggressive autoscaling and warm pools.
- Dedicated: provides predictable headroom and consistent p99 during bursts because we can reserve capacity and pre-warm KV caches; also easier to meet the VPC requirement with a private deployment model.

2) Minimal committed capacity estimate (very rough, pending benchmark):
- If we assume average request costs and cache-hit of 40%: a Dedicated pool sized at ~800–1000 QPS buffer (sustained) with a configured burst allowance to 2k QPS will hold p99 within target.
- If caching hit ratio improves to 70% the required committed capacity drops to ~450–600 QPS.

3) Pilot proposal (attached pilot-scope.md):
- 2-week microbenchmark simulating the burst pattern you shared (we'll run both Hosted and Dedicated profiles):
  * Week 1: run on Hosted with warm pool + autoscale policy tuned to your burst cadence; capture p95/p99 and tail behavior.
  * Week 2: run on a Dedicated reserved pool with pre-warmed KV cache to measure delta and p99 stability.
- Deliverable: one-page recommendation, a cost delta table (hosted vs dedicated committed + burst), and an ops runbook for fallbacks.

4) Asks from your side:
- Access to a 1-hour sample of anonymized request logs (to validate cache-hit assumptions) or a small telemetry dump we can replay.
- Confirmation of us-east region (we have capacity and can guarantee latency SLOs for this region).

We can produce a rough cost ballpark by 3/16 if we get the logs by EOD 3/11. Lauren — I'll coordinate the benchmark and the scope doc; Sanjay — can you confirm who on your team will share the logs and the best way to transfer them (S3 link or secure upload)?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: pilot-scope.md
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@fastledger.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform@fastledger.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deploy mode needs: traffic shape & latency targets

Ben / Lauren —

Got it. We're comfortable sharing a 1-hour anonymized telemetry dump via an S3 presigned URL. I'll have our infra engineer (platform@fastledger.com) upload by EOD 3/11. Confirming: us-east is fine.

Two asks from our side to make the pilot procurement-friendly:
- Can you include an "emergency burst" clause in the pilot scope that allows brief overage for production-like bursts during the test window?
- We need a one-page cost delta (monthly committed vs hosted pay-as-you-go) that we can circulate to procurement.

If you can hit the 3/16 cost ballpark and the pilot scope next week we can aim for the PO by 4/10.

Thanks — looking forward to the bench results.

Sanjay
